definitions.explanation: An individual item or point in a list, document, or set of rules. Most commonly seen in the compound {箇条書|かじょうが}き (bullet-point list).

examples.japanese: {箇条書|かじょうが}きでまとめる。
{要点|ようてん}を{箇条書|かじょうが}きにして{提出|ていしゅつ}してください。
examples.english: Please list the key points in bullet form and submit them.

examples.japanese: {五箇条|ごかじょう}の{御誓文|ごせいもん}は、{明治|めいじ}{政府|せいふ}の{基本方針|きほんほうしん}を{示|しめ}した{文書|ぶんしょ}だ。
examples.english: The Charter Oath of Five Articles was a document setting out the basic policies of the Meiji government.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in the compound {箇条書|かじょうが}き (writing in listed items, bullet points), which is an essential word for business and academic Japanese. Also appears in historical terms like {五箇条|ごかじょう}の{御誓文|ごせいもん} (Charter Oath of Five Articles, 1868).

WRITING:
Also written {ヶ条|かじょう} or か{条|じょう}. The {箇|か} kanji is sometimes replaced with the smaller ヶ.

WATCH OUT:
Not to be confused with {過剰|かじょう} (excess, surplus).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {箇条書|かじょうが}き: bullet-point list
- {五箇条|ごかじょう}: five articles
- {数箇条|すうかじょう}: several items/articles
